description:
University lecturer and science enthusiast with interests in planetary exploration, scientific communication, data visualization, and educational technologies.

Our team is developing an interactive Mars exploration experience based on NASA and ESA mission data from Jezero Crater. The project combines route planning, scientific objectives, hazard assessment, decision-making scenarios, and immersive 360° views to help users experience a simulated astronaut traverse on Mars.
summary:
EVA-01: Jezero Delta Explorer is an interactive Marswalk planning experience designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map."
The project guides users through a proposed astronaut traverse across scientifically important locations within Jezero Crater, the landing site of NASA's Perseverance rover. Through an interactive mission map, users explore six key destinations, analyze geological features, assess hazards, make mission decisions, access immersive 360° views based on real Mars data, and learn how scientists investigate ancient environments on the Red Planet.
Our solution addresses the challenge by transforming complex planetary datasets into an intuitive exploration and decision-making tool for future human explorers. Rather than presenting Mars data in isolation, the project integrates route planning, scientific objectives, sample collection, and environmental observations into a coherent mission experience.
By combining education, storytelling, and authentic NASA and ESA resources, EVA-01 helps users better understand the opportunities and challenges of conducting scientific exploration on Mars.
details:
EVA-01: Jezero Delta Explorer is an interactive Marswalk planning experience that helps users explore one of the most scientifically important regions on Mars: Jezero Crater, the landing site of NASA's Perseverance rover. Inspired by the challenge goal of creating a map that supports future human exploration, our project combines navigation, scientific context, hazard awareness, and immersive exploration into a single experience.

The application is centered around a mission map representing a proposed astronaut traverse through six key locations. Users can select exploration sites, review mission objectives, assess terrain and scientific value, examine hazards, and make exploration decisions. Each location includes educational content explaining its geological significance and links to immersive 360° environments built from real Mars mission imagery. After completing the traverse, users receive a mission debrief and can even listen to authentic sounds recorded on Mars by NASA's Perseverance rover.

The project's primary benefit is transforming complex planetary science data into an intuitive exploration experience that is accessible to students, educators, and the general public. Rather than simply displaying maps or images, EVA-01 presents Mars exploration as a sequence of decisions similar to those future astronauts may face during a real Marswalk.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, image editing tools, NASA resources, ESA panoramic visualizations, and publicly available Mars mission data. The interactive route map, educational storytelling, color-coded mission structure, and integration of immersive panoramic exploration create a unique experience that bridges scientific information and human-centered exploration planning.

Throughout development, we considered usability, educational value, scientific accuracy, visual clarity, accessibility, and the need to communicate complex exploration concepts in a way that is engaging and easy to understand. The result is a lightweight, web-based prototype that demonstrates how future explorers could plan, navigate, and better understand a scientifically rich region of Mars.
